Frame: adjacent-vertical (probability 0.12)
Title: Strava Segments for Skill Journeys
Thesis: Alumni CLR journeys become followable 'segments' first-years pace against, with Copilot surfacing the right alum at the right week.
Why this frame: Strava and Peloton proved that *temporal* benchmarking — 'where were you at this point?' — beats static comparison. Translating that pattern into the CLR domain reframes alumni from intimidating one-shot mentors into longitudinal pacers anchored to specific weeks of a shared journey, dissolving the awkwardness of cold outreach.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Priya Ramaswamy
  Role: First-year Computer Engineering undergraduate, Northeastern University
  Context: Six weeks into her first semester, struggling through CS2500 (Fundamentals of Computer Science I) while watching peers who took AP CS in high school move twice as fast. Has logged six CLR competency events so far — three technical, three behavioral — and her advisor flagged her trajectory as 'foundational but at-risk for the data-fluency track.' She lives in Teams for coursework and only opens NUworks under duress.
  Emotional state: Quietly anxious. Performs confidence in class but Googles 'is it too late to switch majors' at 1am. Energized by visible progress (closes Apple Watch rings religiously) but deflated by the opacity of where she 'should' be by week 6.
  Pain points:
    - No sense of whether her current pace is normal, behind, or ahead — every advisor conversation feels like reading tea leaves.
    - Alumni outreach platforms feel like cold-calling strangers at brand-name companies who graduated a decade ago and don't remember being lost.
    - CLR feels like a compliance checkbox rather than a navigational tool — competency entries disappear into a void.
    - Co-op feels two years away and abstract; she has no week-by-week ritual that connects today's struggle to a co-op outcome.
  JTBD: When I'm in the middle of a hard week and unsure if I'm falling behind, I want to see exactly where people like me were at this same week and what they did next, so I can stop catastrophizing and take the next visible step.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Alumni Pacer (recent grad, 1-5 years out): Opts into 'micro-volunteering' as a pacer for one or more CLR segments. Receives Copilot-drafted week-aligned check-in prompts in Teams; spends ~10 min/week.
  - Co-op Advisor (Coach View): Monitors anonymized cohort trajectories, identifies stalled students, flags pacer matches that need human oversight.
  - Liz (Program Owner): Approves segment templates and pacer communication tone; named in chrome as approver on every outbound template.
  - IT M365 Admin: Owns the SharePoint CLR index, Azure OpenAI vector store, and Power Automate flows.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Priya opens her Trajectory Canvas in Teams on a Wednesday afternoon. Her path renders as a luminous motion line through six completed CLR milestones. Three pacer alumni avatars hover two weeks ahead of her on the Python-to-data-fluency segment. One — Sarah, now at a climate-tech co-op — has just sent a week-6 Teams nudge: 'Week 6 was when I almost dropped the major. Here's what I wish someone had told me.'

USE CASES (11) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Skill Trajectory Visualization
     Trigger: Priya opens the Trajectory Canvas tab inside her Teams sidebar for the first time on a Monday morning.
     Flow: Canvas renders her six logged CLR competency events as nodes on a horizontal motion-line path. Each node shows the competency tag (e.g., 'Recursion fluency', 'Team retro participation') and the week it was logged. Faded ghost-nodes ahead mark anticipated milestones drawn from the segment template. A subtle pace indicator shows her position relative to the median first-year trajectory for her declared track.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro embeds each CLR event into the segment-template vector space and computes a temporal-similarity position. Claude generates a one-sentence 'state of your week' headline grounded in her last three events.
     Outcome: Priya sees, for the first time, that her path is *legible* — not behind, not ahead, but *somewhere specific*. The anxiety of opacity drops; she starts treating CLR as a map rather than a checklist.
  2. Pacer Alumni Recommendations
     Trigger: Priya taps the 'Find Pacers' affordance on her Trajectory Canvas.
     Flow: System surfaces 3-5 alumni avatars positioned two-to-four weeks ahead of her on the same segment. Each card shows the alum's first-year trajectory miniaturized, the specific week where their path intersected with hers, and the week-by-week story of how they got from her current state to two weeks ahead.
     AI role: Azure OpenAI semantic vector search over SharePoint-indexed alumni CLR histories, filtered by temporal alignment (similar week-6 state) and segment overlap. Claude composes the 'why this pacer, why now' explanation card.
     Outcome: Priya picks Sarah — not because Sarah is the most credentialed alum, but because Sarah was *exactly* where Priya is now and is two weeks ahead on the path Priya wants to walk.
  3. Subscribe to a Segment (8-week cadence)
     Trigger: Priya taps 'Pace with Sarah' on Sarah's pacer card.
     Flow: Subscribe modal opens: shows the 8-week segment plan, the cadence of Teams nudges (weekly check-ins, two milestone celebrations, one mid-segment retro), Sarah's expected commitment (10 min/week), and the FERPA double-opt-in disclosure. Priya confirms; Power Automate triggers a kickoff Teams chat with a Copilot-drafted intro message naming the specific shared week-6 struggle.
     AI role: Claude drafts the kickoff intro grounded in the matched temporal slice. Power Automate schedules the 8-week nudge cadence. Gemini generates each week's question seed in advance.
     Outcome: Priya now has a structured 8-week relationship with predictable rhythm, low friction for both sides, and a built-in graceful exit at week 8.
  4. Week-by-Week Copilot Nudges
     Trigger: Every Tuesday at 4pm during the active segment, Power Automate fires a weekly nudge into the Priya-Sarah Teams chat.
     Flow: Nudge surfaces as a Copilot card inside the chat: 'Week 7 of your segment. Sarah, in your week 7 you logged the GitHub-collab milestone. Priya, want to share where you are on collaborative coding this week?' Both parties can tap suggested replies, free-form, or snooze.
     AI role: Claude generates the nudge copy anchored to the pacer's historical week-N CLR event. Gemini ranks 3 suggested replies for each party that match their communication style based on prior chat history.
     Outcome: The relationship stays warm with near-zero overhead. Sarah feels useful in 90 seconds; Priya feels held without feeling watched.
  5. Pacer Check-In Prompts (Copilot-guided)
     Trigger: Sarah opens Teams and sees a Copilot prompt suggesting a week-aligned check-in for Priya.
     Flow: Copilot offers three pre-drafted, professionally-toned check-ins ('Curious how the recursion problem set landed', 'Want to share the GitHub flow that saved me in week 7', 'Just checking in — week 7 was rough for me too'). Sarah picks one, optionally edits, sends. Liz's approved template style is enforced by a tone-guardrail.
     AI role: Claude generates check-in variants in Liz-approved tone register. A safety classifier flags any draft that strays from the approved communication template.
     Outcome: Sarah's 'I should reach out' guilt is replaced by a 2-tap action. Risk of inappropriate or off-tone outreach is intercepted at draft time.
  6. Trajectory Milestone Celebrations
     Trigger: Priya logs a CLR event that matches a milestone on the active segment (e.g., 'first PR merged on a team repo').
     Flow: Canvas animates the milestone node lighting up. A celebration card appears in the Teams chat: confetti motion, the milestone name, and a contextual line: 'This is the same milestone Sarah hit in her week 8 — she remembers it as the moment things clicked.' Optional reaction prompts.
     AI role: Gemini Imagen generates a custom celebration illustration grounded in the milestone theme. Claude writes the contextualization line tying the milestone to the pacer's history.
     Outcome: Progress becomes emotionally salient and shared. Priya gets the closed-ring dopamine she craves; Sarah gets to witness it.
  7. Cohort Comparison (anonymized)
     Trigger: Priya taps 'How am I tracking?' on the Canvas.
     Flow: An anonymized cohort overlay renders: a translucent band showing the 25th-75th percentile path for first-years on her declared segment. Her line is positioned within or near the band. No individual peers identifiable; FERPA cohort-minimum (n≥10) enforced.
     AI role: Embeddings cluster cohort trajectories; a FERPA cohort-anonymization safeguard refuses to render any view where n<10 or where any individual could be re-identified.
     Outcome: Priya can answer 'am I normal?' without surveilling specific peers. Anxiety is calibrated, not amplified.
  8. Coach View for Co-op Advisors
     Trigger: Priya's advisor opens the Coach View tab during weekly caseload review.
     Flow: Advisor sees a sortable list of advisees with trajectory health indicators (on-pace, drifting, stalled, accelerating), active pacer status, and last-touch dates. Tapping a student opens an anonymized version of their Canvas plus the active segment subscriptions. Advisor can request a hand-off conversation but cannot read pacer DMs (FERPA boundary).
     AI role: Gemini scores trajectory health weekly; Claude composes a one-line 'what to ask Priya about this week' suggestion for the advisor.
     Outcome: Advisors shift from reactive matchmaking to proactive coaching at scale; they see the system's work without intruding on the student-pacer relationship.
  9. Pacer Bandwidth Throttling
     Trigger: A popular pacer (e.g., Sarah) approaches her opted-in capacity of 3 active segments.
     Flow: When a fourth student tries to subscribe, the system gracefully defers: 'Sarah is at capacity this term — here are two alumni with very similar week-6 trajectories who have bandwidth.' No notification to Sarah; no rejection to the student.
     AI role: Power Automate enforces capacity rules; Gemini retrieves the top alternative pacers and Claude writes the substitution message preserving warmth.
     Outcome: Pacer burnout is structurally impossible; students never see 'rejected' framing.
  10. Mid-Segment Retro (Week 4)
     Trigger: At week 4 of the active segment, Power Automate triggers a retro card in the Teams chat.
     Flow: Card asks both parties three short questions (what's working, what's stuck, change cadence?). Responses are private to the pair plus aggregated anonymously for Liz's program-quality dashboard.
     AI role: Claude generates personalized retro questions grounded in the actual chat history of the prior four weeks.
     Outcome: Course-correction happens before disengagement; Liz gets program-level signal without surveillance.
  11. Graceful Segment Completion
     Trigger: Week 8 nudge fires the segment-completion card.
     Flow: Card celebrates the journey, asks each party to optionally endorse a competency on the other's CLR, offers Priya a curated next-segment recommendation, and offers Sarah a low-friction 'pace another student' button or a clean 'take a term off' opt-out.
     AI role: Gemini recommends the next segment based on Priya's now-updated trajectory; Claude drafts the endorsement language.
     Outcome: Relationships end well, not by ghosting; CLR records get peer-endorsed evidence; the next loop is teed up without coercion.

KEY SCREENS (10) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Trajectory Canvas — purpose: The persistent home view inside Teams: Priya's CLR journey rendered as a motion-line path with completed nodes, anticipated ghost-nodes, and pacer avatars positioned ahead of her.
     Primary element: A horizontal scrollable canvas with a glowing path line, week markers across the bottom, competency nodes along the path, and translucent pacer avatars at their time-aligned positions.
     Motion character: Slow continuous drift on the motion line (like a Strava heatmap pulse), gentle parallax when scrolling weeks, pacer avatars subtly breathe.
  2. Pacer Detail with Time-Aligned Match — purpose: Deep-dive on a specific pacer alum, showing exactly where their path intersected with the student's and what the next two weeks of their journey looked like.
     Primary element: Split view: pacer's miniaturized trajectory on the left highlighting the matched week, a narrative panel on the right with the AI-composed 'why this match, why now' explanation grounded in shared competency events.
     Motion character: On open, both trajectories animate in and a connecting arc draws between the matched week points; smooth, deliberate, 600ms.
  3. Subscribe-to-Segment Modal — purpose: The double-opt-in moment where Priya commits to an 8-week paced relationship and the FERPA disclosure is surfaced.
     Primary element: An 8-step timeline preview, expected weekly time commitment for each side, FERPA double-opt-in checkbox, Liz-approved-template badge, and a single 'Pace with Sarah' confirm button.
     Motion character: Modal lifts from the pacer card with a spring transition; the 8 weeks fan out sequentially as a reveal.
  4. Weekly Teams Nudge Thread — purpose: The recurring Tuesday-4pm Copilot-card-in-Teams that keeps the relationship warm with structure.
     Primary element: An adaptive Copilot card embedded in the chat: week number, pacer's historical event, prompt question, three suggested replies, snooze affordance.
     Motion character: Card slides in from top of chat; suggested-reply chips have a tactile press animation; sending dissolves the card into a normal chat bubble.
  5. Milestone Celebration Card — purpose: Mark a CLR milestone that lines up with a segment node — an emotional checkpoint shared between Priya and Sarah.
     Primary element: Full-width Teams card with a custom Imagen-generated illustration, the milestone name, a contextual line tying it to the pacer's history, and reaction emoji.
     Motion character: Confetti particle burst on first view; the corresponding canvas node lights up and pulses three times.
  6. Anonymized Cohort Comparison — purpose: Let Priya benchmark her pace against an anonymized first-year cohort without identifying any specific peer.
     Primary element: Translucent percentile band overlaid on her Canvas (25th-75th), with a soft 'n=247' badge confirming cohort minimum was respected.
     Motion character: Band fades in over 800ms; a small toast asserts the FERPA safeguard ('cohort anonymized, n≥10 enforced').
  7. Advisor Coach View — purpose: The advisor's caseload dashboard showing trajectory health across advisees with appropriate FERPA boundaries.
     Primary element: A list/grid of advisees with trajectory-health pill badges, active-pacer indicators, last-touch dates, and a 'this week's coaching prompt' panel powered by Claude.
     Motion character: Quiet, data-dense, minimal animation — feels like a clinical decision-support tool, not a consumer app.
  8. Pacer Mission Control (alumnus view) — purpose: Sarah's view of her active mentees, her capacity meter, this week's Copilot-drafted prompts, and her own commitment runway.
     Primary element: Three active-mentee cards with the week number and a 2-tap 'send check-in' action; capacity meter at top (3/3 active); 'Take next term off' graceful-exit button.
     Motion character: Calm and efficient; everything fits in a single Teams-tab viewport, no scroll.
  9. FERPA & Consent Center — purpose: Centralized view of what data is shared, with whom, and for how long — auditable and revocable.
     Primary element: A list of active consents with timestamps, scope description in plain language, and a one-tap revoke action; explicit double-opt-in lineage shown.
     Motion character: Static, formal, document-like; reassuring rather than playful.
  10. Liz's Program Quality Dashboard (Power BI embed) — purpose: Program owner's view of segment subscriptions, pacer engagement rates, retro signals, and the 50% alumni-engagement KPI.
     Primary element: Embedded Power BI tiles: subscription funnel, week-by-week retention, pacer satisfaction, advisor escalations.
     Motion character: Standard Power BI chrome — deliberately stack-native to honor Jen's mandate.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Time-Aligned Trajectory Similarity
     User action: Priya opens the Trajectory Canvas or taps 'Find Pacers'.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Priya's CLR event stream (timestamps, competency tags, evidence artifacts) + alumni CLR histories indexed in SharePoint with embedded segment annotations.
     Output: A ranked list of alumni whose week-N state most resembles Priya's current state, with a position offset (e.g., 'two weeks ahead on Python-to-data-fluency segment'). Falls back to Claude Opus 4.7 if Gemini call fails.
     User benefit: Matches feel uncannily relevant because they're matched on *when* and *how*, not just *what*.
  2. Headline Aha Explanation Composer
     User action: Priya opens a pacer detail card.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The matched week's shared competency events for both Priya and the pacer, the pacer's subsequent two-week trajectory, and Liz's approved tone register.
     Output: A 2-3 sentence explanation grounded in specific shared evidence: 'I connected you because in week 6 you both hit the recursion wall, and Sarah's path from here led to a fintech co-op two semesters later.' Uses Verbalized Sampling to generate 3 candidate phrasings and selects the most specific.
     User benefit: This is the headline aha — the moment Priya understands the system *sees* her, not just her profile.
  3. Weekly Nudge Generator
     User action: Tuesday 4pm Power Automate trigger fires for an active segment.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Current segment week, pacer's historical CLR event at that week, last 7 days of chat history, both parties' communication-style fingerprint.
     Output: A Copilot-card nudge with one anchor prompt and three suggested replies for each party, all in Liz-approved tone. Gemini fallback if Claude rate-limited.
     User benefit: Sarah spends 90 seconds/week instead of 30 minutes drafting; Priya gets warm, week-relevant touch with zero awkwardness.
  4. Milestone Detection from CLR Evidence
     User action: Priya logs a new CLR event (PR merged, presentation given, peer endorsement received).
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: The new CLR event payload + active segment template + Priya's prior trajectory.
     Output: A milestone classification (matched / not matched / partial) and, if matched, a celebration trigger payload for the Teams card.
     User benefit: Progress is recognized in real time, not at end-of-semester reviews.
  5. Imagen Celebration Illustrations
     User action: A milestone is detected.
     Model: Gemini Imagen
     Input: Milestone theme, segment name, Northeastern visual register (warm, editorial, athletic-academic).
     Output: A unique celebration illustration for the card — rendered at trigger time, never stock.
     User benefit: Each milestone feels singular; the app earns the small-but-real dopamine moment.
  6. Cohort Anonymization Safeguard
     User action: Priya opens cohort comparison view.
     Model: Embeddings + rule-based guard (custom)
     Input: Cohort trajectory embeddings + cell-size policy (n≥10) + segment-specific re-identification risk score.
     Output: Either an anonymized percentile band rendered, or a graceful refusal: 'This view needs at least 10 students on your segment — check back in 2 weeks.'
     User benefit: FERPA compliance is visible and trustworthy, not invisible and assumed.
  7. Pacer Bandwidth-Aware Throttling
     User action: A student tries to subscribe to an at-capacity pacer.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Pacer capacity state + alternative pacers ranked by time-aligned similarity + recency-of-engagement bonus.
     Output: Top 2 alternative pacers with a Claude-composed substitution message that preserves warmth and never frames the original as rejecting.
     User benefit: Pacer burnout is structurally impossible; the student never feels turned away.
  8. Advisor Weekly Coaching Prompt
     User action: Advisor opens Coach View on Monday morning.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Each advisee's trajectory health signal, active pacer status, recent CLR events, last advisor touch.
     Output: One sentence per advisee: 'Ask Priya about her week-6 recursion block — Sarah's pacing seems to be helping; consider reinforcing.'
     User benefit: Advisors arrive at every conversation already grounded in specific, current signal.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Trajectory-forward editorial restraint with athletic-academic motion vocabulary. Imagine Strava's heatmap energy crossed with the typographic seriousness of a Wired feature — confident motion lines, lots of whitespace, considered typography (NU-aligned serif for headlines, clean sans for UI), warm-but-disciplined palette (charcoal, paper, NU-red as a single accent), zero gratuitous gradient bloat. Microsoft Teams chrome is honored and visible; the experience lives inside it, not despite it.
  Hero treatment: The Trajectory Canvas is the hero. A horizontal motion-line path, gently luminous, runs across the viewport. Completed CLR nodes are solid; anticipated nodes are ghostly; pacer avatars float two-to-four weeks ahead with subtle breathing animation. Above the path, a single-sentence Claude-composed status line in editorial serif. Below the path, week markers in monospace. The canvas feels like a Strava activity map redrawn as an academic transcript that's been given a pulse.
  Motion character: Continuous, breathing, never frantic. Motion lines drift at ~2px/sec; pacer avatars pulse on a 4-second cycle; node activations use spring physics with mild overshoot. Page transitions are continuous-motion handoffs (no cut-cuts). Skeleton states feel like heartbeats. The only fast motion is reserved for milestone celebrations — confetti bursts that earn their excitement.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Imagen prompt: 'Editorial illustration of a student crossing a glowing threshold marked WEEK 6, warm charcoal-and-paper palette with a single accent of crimson, athletic-academic feel, no faces, abstract motion lines suggesting forward momentum.'
    2. Imagen prompt: 'Milestone celebration illustration for first PR merged — abstract Git-branch shape rendered as twin running tracks converging, warm light, editorial restraint, Northeastern crimson accent.'
    3. Imagen prompt: 'Cover hero for Cold-Outreach-to-Confident-Networker segment — an empty conference room chair transforming into an extended hand, monochrome with single crimson accent.'
    4. Imagen prompt: 'Cohort comparison overlay illustration — a translucent crowd of motion-line paths flowing together like a river delta, individual paths illegible to imply anonymization, paper background.'
    5. Imagen prompt: 'Pacer hand-off moment illustration — two motion lines overlapping at a single point in time, one continuing forward, the other peeling off, athletic-academic restraint.'
    6. Imagen prompt: 'Segment completion celebration — a finishing tape moment rendered as the closing of an academic chapter, warm light, NU crimson accent.'

  Goals — life: To leave a legacy of impactful, data-driven educational improvements that genuinely benefit students and the institution.; experience: To feel effective and empowered in driving technological change, seeing tangible results without unnecessary bureaucratic hurdles.; functional: To successfully implement an AI-enabled system for comprehensive learner records and improved co-op matching.
  Voice (verbatim from research): "I could get a comprehensive learner without anybody knowing."
=== GROUNDING THEMES (cited by this concept) ===
  1. Alumni Mentorship and Trailblazer Networks
    Thesis: There is a massive, untapped opportunity to leverage Northeastern's alumni network for peer-to-peer mentorship and co-op opportunity generation. While the current 'NU Source' platform is dysfunctional and unowned, stakeholders agree that alumni strongly identify with the co-op experience and are eager to give back. Connecting current students with 'Trailblazers' who have successfully navigated similar paths is a highly requested feature.

  2. Shift from Placement to Proactive Preparation
    Thesis: The traditional model of co-op advisors acting as personalized job matchmakers is no longer viable given the scale of the student body and the competitiveness of the market. The university is explicitly shifting its stance to clarify that it does not 'place' students; rather, it prepares them to compete. This requires a massive reallocation of resources toward early-stage skill building and portfolio development.
=== RESEARCH GOAL (the engagement question this prototype helps answer) ===
Identify a comprehensive new strategy for co-op based on the current statement of work for NU, prior projects with NU, and fresh industry analysis of experiential learning and co-op engagement tactics to improve learner's chances of gaining meaningful experiential learning opportunities from pre-enrollment to graduate school
=== BUILD INSTRUCTIONS ===
Build a multi-screen experience grounded in the persona's actual pain points above. The downstream pipeline will:
  • Generate 5 distinct product briefs via Verbalized Sampling. The user picks ONE.
  • Author an exhaustive Build Recipe (every screen, every state, every AI prompt, every seed-data anchor, every micro-copy string).
  • Execute the recipe to produce a substantive IDEO/Apple-grade prototype with 4+ screens, 2+ AI fetches via multi-provider fallback, 20+ seed records per primary entity, no verbatim research quotes, and Verbalized Sampling on creative AI output.
Apply industry-agnostic rigor — the same standards regardless of vertical (healthcare, fintech, retail, government, manufacturing, education, etc.). Distill insights from the GROUNDING THEMES and persona voice into the design; never reproduce research quotes verbatim in the prototype UI.

brief.one_line_thesis: Alumni CLR journeys become followable 'segments' first-years pace against, with Copilot surfacing the right alum at the right week.

primary_persona.name: Priya Ramaswamy
primary_persona.context: Six weeks into her first semester, struggling through CS2500 (Fundamentals of Computer Science I) while watching peers who took AP CS in high school move twice as fast. Has logged six CLR competency events so far — three technical, three behavioral — and her advisor flagged her trajectory as 'foundational but at-risk for the data-fluency track.' She lives in Teams for coursework and only opens NUworks under duress.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Quietly anxious. Performs confidence in class but Googles 'is it too late to switch majors' at 1am. Energized by visible progress (closes Apple Watch rings religiously) but deflated by the opacity of where she 'should' be by week 6.

secondary_actors.involvement: Opts into 'micro-volunteering' as a pacer for one or more CLR segments. Receives Copilot-drafted week-aligned check-in prompts in Teams; spends ~10 min/week.
Monitors anonymized cohort trajectories, identifies stalled students, flags pacer matches that need human oversight.
Approves segment templates and pacer communication tone; named in chrome as approver on every outbound template.
Owns the SharePoint CLR index, Azure OpenAI vector store, and Power Automate flows.

brief.demonstrated_moment: Priya opens her Trajectory Canvas in Teams on a Wednesday afternoon. Her path renders as a luminous motion line through six completed CLR milestones. Three pacer alumni avatars hover two weeks ahead of her on the Python-to-data-fluency segment. One — Sarah, now at a climate-tech co-op — has just sent a week-6 Teams nudge: 'Week 6 was when I almost dropped the major. Here's what I wish someone had told me.'
jobs_to_be_done: When I'm in the middle of a hard week and unsure if I'm falling behind, I want to see exactly where people like me were at this same week and what they did next, so I can stop catastrophizing and take the next visible step.
success_criteria: First-year students who subscribe to a segment complete week 4 at ≥70% retention.
Alumni pacers report ≤12 minutes/week time investment and ≥4/5 satisfaction at segment completion.
Alumni engagement rates increase ≥50% vs. the legacy NU Source baseline within two semesters.
Student-reported career confidence increases ≥30% on post-segment survey relative to non-subscribed control.
Zero FERPA incidents; every data flow has a visible double-opt-in consent record in the SharePoint audit log.
Co-op advisors using the Coach View report higher-quality weekly check-ins (qualitative ≥80% positive at semester end).
By Year 2, ≥15% of pilot-cohort first co-ops are sourced through pacer-network referrals (the 'hidden network' KPI).

hard_constraints.brand: Honors Northeastern University visual register (NU crimson as single accent, paper-and-charcoal foundation) and visibly inhabits the Microsoft Teams / Microsoft 365 / SharePoint / Power Automate / Power BI chrome named by Jen. Liz-approved-template badges appear on every outbound communication. No new standalone platform branding — the product lives as a Teams tab and a set of Copilot cards.
other: No verbatim research quotes anywhere in product UI.
FERPA double-opt-in is required and visible before any cross-party data flow.
Pacer capacity throttling enforced — students never see a 'rejection' frame.
All AI text generation uses multi-provider fallback (Claude Opus 4.7 ↔ Gemini 3.1 Pro) and Verbalized Sampling on creative outputs.
Every AI-generated outbound message passes a tone-guardrail classifier aligned to Liz-approved templates.
Existing systems (NUworks, Canvas, Banner, M365) are reused; no new platform procurement.

critique.summary: 100% session coverage (simulated). The prototype successfully implements the core Trajectory Canvas and Teams Chat Nudge flows, with robust multi-provider AI fallbacks and dense seed data. However, it misses several critical accessibility floor requirements (focus traps, aria-labels, reduced motion) and fails to persist state to sessionStorage as mandated by the cross-cutting spec.
